clue.text: Gin served in cardboard container available at Terminal 5 …

definitions.note: a boarding pass is the card holder's ticket to the plane, carried at Heathrow's Terminal 5

indicators.note: gin that is served is dished out and splashed about, so its letters are mixed in with the others

explanation.surface: A measure of gin poured into a paper cup at the airport bar before a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GIN and CARDBOARD together rearrange into the answer; 'in' just joins the two parts of the fodder. Terminal 5 is the British Airways terminal at London Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass of stiff card handed out at airport check-in, needed before getting on the aircraft, is an item found at any airport terminal.

clue.text: Article provided by airline for dipping in water

indicators.note: the article is supplied by, so comes after, the airline

parts.note: BA is British Airways
an article is a thing, any object

explanation.surface: An airline hands out something for passengers to use while swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like grammar (a, the) but here it is just an object, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Going for a swim or plunging into a pool is bathing, the act of dipping oneself.

clue.text: A head teacher minds and listens

indicators.note: the head of the teacher is that word's first letter

parts.note: to mind something is to tend it, look after it

explanation.surface: A head teacher looks after the pupils and pays heed to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head teacher' reads as a headmaster, but 'head' takes only the teacher's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to someone is to listen to them and pay heed, so attends means listens.

clue.text: Push girl's mass volume

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the girl's is DI'S
a missal is the book used for saying Mass

explanation.surface: Shove aside the young woman's heavy tome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The push' is informal for being sacked, as in 'given the push'.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the push is slang for being fired, which is a dismissal from one's job.

clue.text: Push girl's top with nothing on

indicators.note: the girl's top letter goes together with, inside, the bare word

parts.note: with nothing on is naked, nude

indicators.note: the top of the word girl's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shove a girl whose top is off and who wears nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: G (girl's top) goes into NUDE, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle push with the elbow is a nudge, a small prod.

clue.text: Jesuitic flower?

parts.note: names a wild flower that shares its name with a sainted Elizabethan Jesuit martyr, the flower of the Jesuit order

explanation.definitionFit: Saint Edmund Campion was an English Jesuit martyr, and the campion is a pink or white wild flower.

clue.text: Wine container with top off overturned

indicators.note: a down entry turned over is read bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
the container loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: a canister is a container, a tin or box

explanation.surface: Wine whose container has lost its lid and been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: CANISTER without its top is ANISTER; 'overturned' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Actor caught between drinks

indicators.note: caught sits between the two drinks

parts.note: ale is one drink
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Guinness, the Irish stout, is the other drink

explanation.surface: A performer nabbed between pints at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Guinness was an English film and stage actor, famous for Star Wars and Kind Hearts and Coronets.

clue.text: … a little of it fills Porkie's figure

indicators.note: the small measure fills the falsehoods, going inside them

parts.note: porkies, from rhyming slang porky pies, are lies
a tot is a little of it, the gin of the run-on clue

explanation.surface: A drop of gin is poured into the shape of the liar.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 1 across, so 'it' is the gin there. Porky pies is British rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech: understatement by denying the opposite, such as 'not bad'.

clue.text: Popular rally gets involuntary response

parts.note: a rally or protest march is a demo
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A protest gathering provokes a reflex reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of or for the ordinary people, common and colloquial, so popular in the old sense.

clue.text: End court shoe fashion with a plonk

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or form anew, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Finish a court-shoe trend with a cheap glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court shoe' is a British name for a plain women's pump; 'fashion' is a verb here, not footwear trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Côtes du Rhône is an everyday red wine, and plonk is slang for cheap wine.

clue.text: Character against drink

parts.note: chi is a letter, or character, of the Greek alphabet
anti means against

explanation.surface: A person of principle set against alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is an Italian red wine from Tuscany, so a drink.

clue.text: Titles one devised for top people

indicators.note: to devise is to work out anew, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Honours dreamed up for the great and good.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitist describes things meant for or favouring an elite, the top people of society.

clue.text: Eggs needed in our gestation process

indicators.note: the letters are found in the words our gestation, run together

explanation.surface: Eggs are needed while a baby develops in the womb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs' looks like a noun about reproduction, but it is the verb 'eggs on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them, so eggs means urges.

clue.text: Drunks are about, even here

indicators.note: the drunks are about, around, the next word

parts.note: soaks are heavy drinkers, drunks

explanation.surface: Even in this place the town drunks are everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENOAKS is a commuter town in Kent; 'here' asks for the place the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue as a whole sets the scene in a town, and 'here' points to that place.

clue.text: Inverse tail wagging is adaptable

indicators.note: a tail that is wagging moves about, so its letters are shaken around

parts.note: read as 'in verse', the word gives verse after a link 'in'

explanation.surface: A tail wagging the wrong way is flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius means 'Inverse' to be read as two words, 'In verse', with 'In' only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile means able to adapt to many uses or roles, so adaptable.

clue.text: Leader like Roosevelt

parts.note: the word leader is a new form of dealer, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A head of state in the style of Franklin D. Roosevelt.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Deal was Roosevelt's 1930s economic programme; its backers were New Dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Dealer was a supporter of Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal, so politically like him.

clue.text: Gate was broken, leading to loss of stock

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A broken gate lets the cattle escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is loss through waste or leakage, as of goods or stock.

clue.text: Made to do a stretch with possibility of remission

definitions.text: Made to do a stretch with possibility of remission

parts.words: Made to do a stretch with possibility of remission
parts.note: reads like a prison term that might be cut short, but describes a band built to stretch and then spring back

explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material is made to stretch and then recover, and 'stretch' is slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Lost or died in a foreign land

definitions.meaning: the word is borrowed from French and means lost or hidden from view
a person lost, gone out of sight

explanation.definitionFit: Perdu, from French, means lost, out of sight, gone for good.

clue.text: Italian governor could be a despot

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged to form another word

explanation.surface: An Italian ruler who might be a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A podestà was the chief magistrate or governor of a medieval Italian town.

clue.text: Uncommon feature of British society

parts.note: reads as a rarity, but describes those who are literally not commoners in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The Crown and royal family are a distinctive part of British society, and royals are not commoners.

clue.text: Eyes cast around with leader lost in rapture

indicators.note: the letters are turned around, put into a new order
the word eyes loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone looks about, beside themselves with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'around' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is overwhelming joy or delight, a state of rapture.

clue.text: Long story without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the story goes outside the point

parts.note: a yarn is a tale or story
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A long tale that has no point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its older sense it means outside, so YARN goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it; both are verbs of desire.

clue.text: Ancient crone speaking in theatre

indicators.note: speaking means the words are said aloud

parts.note: an ancient crone is an old witch

explanation.surface: An old hag delivering lines on a West End stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The ALDWYCH is a theatre in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aldwych Theatre is a West End playhouse on the street of the same name in London.

clue.text: Quiet car in holy writ

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
the Astra is a Vauxhall car model

explanation.surface: A hush falls in the car while scripture is read.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vauxhall Astra is a common British family car.
explanation.definitionFit: A shastra is a Hindu sacred text, a scripture or holy writ.

clue.text: Endless slur in medical prescription

indicators.note: the slur loses its end, its last letter

parts.note: a slur is an insult

explanation.surface: An unending insult turns up on a doctor's note.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is a hormone prescribed by doctors to treat diabetes.

clue.text: Celebration of Johnson's article in recent "Network Rail"

annotationWithheld.why: Celebration of Johnson's article in recent "Network Rail": wordplay splits the single word Network into NET (fodder) and work (anagram indicator), one word doing two jobs; A + RECENT + NET anagrammed, + RY
annotationWithheld.clue: Celebration of Johnson's article in recent "Network Rail"
